708389.t: From Proto-Hellenic *məňňómai, from Proto-Indo-European *mn̥yétor (“to think”), from *men-. Cognates include Sanskrit मन्य॑ते (mányate), Old Church Slavonic мьнѣти (mĭněti), Old Irish ·muinethar, and Lithuanian miniu.

708377.t: From μαθ- (măth-, root of μανθάνω (mănthắnō, “to learn”)) + -μα (-mă, result noun suffix).

708352.t: From Proto-Indo-European *meh₂d-. Cognates include Sanskrit मद॑ति (mádati), म॒मत्ति॑ (mamátti), Latin madeō, and Old Irish maidid.

708344.t: Perhaps from Pre-Greek. Compare also μάχαιρα (mákhaira, “large sword”).

708381.t: Possibly the same root as μήτηρ (mḗtēr).
